methodology: Independently constructed 8 fresh adversarial fixture groups, distinct from Workstream D's own 9-case matrix (tests/contract-model/claim-identity-v2.test.ts) and from the prior BLOCKER-8 certification's 8-case matrix (tests/foundation-audit/section15-claim-identity-adversarial.ts) - though the original F15-1 collision sentence is deliberately REUSED verbatim for the regression check (task requirement 5). Every fixture is run through the REAL, unmodified, currently-deployed production functions: runPassCNeighborhoodExpansion + runPassDReconciliation (discovery layer: discoveryId/candidateRef) and hypothesizeUnitsForDocument (semantic-coverage layer: semanticUnitId) - never re-derived stand-ins. SemanticRuleItem inputs are constructed directly (Pass B's own output shape), matching the same LLM-bypass technique every predecessor claim-identity test file in this codebase already established, since no LLM API key is configured in this environment. All fixtures and their exact resolved identities are captured in tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-blocker8-adversarial.test.ts (23 tests, all passing against current, unmodified production code) and reproduced narratively below.

task1_freshAdversarialConstruction.purpose: Attempt to falsify Workstream D's claims using sentence shapes its own 9-case matrix never tried: (a) three (not two) distinct baskets in one sentence; (b) genuinely different value TYPES (dollar vs ratio) fused together; (c) a DATE fused in as a would-be distinguishing signal; (d) a hallucinated number in an AI-authored description.

results.construction: (a) THREE fused same-family Indebtedness baskets, no lettered markers, three distinct dollar figures
results.sentence: The Company may incur Indebtedness in an amount not to exceed $50,000,000, or incur Indebtedness in an amount not to exceed $30,000,000, or incur Indebtedness in an amount not to exceed $20,000,000, in each case for general corporate purposes.
results.discoveryLayerResult: RESOLVED - 3 well-formed SemanticRuleItems (simulating correct Pass B output, one per basket) independently ground their own dollar figure and produce 3 distinct discoveryIds. The discovery layer's per-item grounding design has no N-ary limitation.
results.coverageLayerResult: FALSIFIED CLAIM - only 2 MaterialSemanticUnits are produced, not 3. findCoordinateClauseSplit finds the FIRST qualifying top-level and/or split point ($50M | rest) and returns immediately - it never recurses into the 'rest' text to find the SECOND split point between the $30M and $20M baskets, which therefore remain fused into ONE semanticUnitId despite each stating its own distinct, source-grounded dollar figure. See task2_newFindingDetail below - this is reported as a genuine new finding, not merely a passing/failing test.

results.construction: (a-cross) THREE fused, cross-family (Liens / Indebtedness / Investments) baskets, no lettered markers, three distinct dollar figures - checked to determine whether the N-ary gap is specific to the same-family branch this workstream added, or is a pre-existing limitation of findCoordinateClauseSplit's single-split design shared by the cross-family branch this workstream did NOT modify
results.sentence: The Company shall not create Liens on the Collateral in excess of $5,000,000, or incur Indebtedness in excess of $10,000,000, or make Investments in excess of $15,000,000.
results.coverageLayerResult: Same gap reproduces: only 2 units (LIENS, and a combined INDEBTEDNESS+INVESTMENTS unit). This confirms the single-split limitation is a PRE-EXISTING property of findCoordinateClauseSplit's algorithm shape (return-on-first-match, no recursion), NOT something Workstream D introduced - Workstream D's own change (the same-family branch) inherits, but did not cause, this limitation.
results.verdict: Confirms the gap is structural to the coordinate-clause-split algorithm itself, present in both the pre-existing cross-family branch and the new same-family branch.

results.construction: (b) Genuinely different value TYPES fused together (dollar cap vs leverage-ratio cap), same family/role/node
results.sentence: The Company may incur Indebtedness not to exceed $75,000,000 in the aggregate, or incur Indebtedness so long as after giving effect thereto the Consolidated Leverage Ratio does not exceed 3.50 to 1.00.
results.discoveryLayerResult: RESOLVED - 2 distinct discoveryIds (usd: vs ratio: tagged anchors are trivially disjoint by tag prefix alone, so a same-family clause fusing a currency cap with a ratio-based test correctly splits).
results.coverageLayerResult: RESOLVED - 2 distinct semanticUnitIds via the same value-anchor-disjoint mechanism.
results.verdict: CLAIM HOLDS - the anchor-tagging scheme (usd:/pct:/ratio:) generalizes correctly across value TYPES, not merely across different amounts of the same type.

results.construction: (c) A DATE (not currency/%/ratio) fused into an otherwise-identical same-family sentence, checking whether a date is mistakenly treated as a distinguishing anchor (false positive) or correctly ignored
results.sentence: The Company may incur Indebtedness maturing prior to December 31, 2030, or incur Indebtedness maturing after January 1, 2031.
results.directUnitCheck: extractValueAnchors('December 31, 2030') === [] ; extractValueAnchors('maturing after January 1, 2031') === [] ; extractGroundedValueAnchors(...) === [] - CURRENCY_RE requires a $/£/€ prefix, PERCENTAGE_RE requires a %, RATIO_RE requires an 'x'/'to 1'/':1' suffix. Bare calendar-date digits satisfy none of these three grammars, so no false-positive anchor is ever extracted from a date.
results.coverageLayerResult: Correctly does NOT split (1 unit) - no numeric anchor exists on either side to compare, so valueAnchorSetsDisjointAndNonEmpty correctly returns false (both empty).
results.verdict: CLAIM HOLDS - no false-positive risk from dates. This non-split falls precisely within the ALREADY-DISCLOSED AUDIT-F4-RESIDUAL-1 boundary ('neither side states any numeric/currency/percentage/ratio value') - it is not a broader, undisclosed gap; it is exactly the disclosed gap's own stated shape, independently reconfirmed with a fresh, real-world-plausible sentence (differing maturity dates) the original disclosure never explicitly named.

results.construction: (d) A HALLUCINATED number in Pass B's own (simulated) AI-authored description, absent from the real source text
results.sentence_source: Indebtedness in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $50,000,000 shall be permitted.
results.description_candidate: a hallucinated $99,000,000 basket that does not exist in the real source
results.directUnitCheck: extractGroundedValueAnchors('a hallucinated $99,000,000 basket', sourceText) === [] - the fabricated figure is silently dropped, never trusted.
results.endToEndCheck: The resulting DiscoveredCandidate.valueAnchors === [] (empty) - the hallucinated figure never reaches the identity fingerprint at all.
results.secondaryCheck: Two candidates whose descriptions EACH correctly cite the real $50,000,000 figure alongside their OWN independent hallucinated noise ($77,000,000 and $33,000,000 respectively, never appearing in either the other candidate's description or the source) still ground identically to ['usd:50000000'] and correctly merge into 1 candidate - confirming hallucinated noise never prevents a genuine duplicate from merging, nor does it fabricate a false distinguishing signal between two candidates.
results.verdict: CLAIM HOLDS - extractGroundedValueAnchors genuinely rejects hallucinated numbers rather than trusting them, exactly as documented.

task2_newFindingDetail.title: findCoordinateClauseSplit performs at most ONE split per region - a sentence fusing THREE OR MORE independently-operative claims (same-family or cross-family) with no lettered/numbered sub-reference is only partially separated, silently re-conflating the 2nd and every subsequent fused claim into a single MaterialSemanticUnit/semanticUnitId
task2_newFindingDetail.severity: MODERATE - narrower than the ORIGINAL BLOCKER-8 defect (which affected the common 2-way case) but squarely inside AUDIT-F4's own frozen defect class ('SAME FAMILY + SAME ROLE + SAME SOURCE NODE DOES NOT IMPLY SAME CLAIM'), and NOT the disclosed AUDIT-F4-RESIDUAL-1 (which requires ZERO number on both remaining sides - the conflated claims here each carry their own distinct, source-grounded, mutually-disjoint number).
task2_newFindingDetail.mechanism: findCoordinateClauseSplit (lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-coverage/unit-hypothesis.ts) scans left-to-right through every top-level and/or occurrence and RETURNS on the FIRST candidate whose two sides independently qualify (different family, or same family with disjoint value anchors). It never recurses into either the returned left.text or right.text to search for a SECOND qualifying split point. hypothesizeUnitsForRegion (the sole caller) treats the function's return as final - it builds exactly leftUnit and rightUnit and returns, with no further splitting pass over either half.
task2_newFindingDetail.reproduction: tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-blocker8-adversarial.test.ts, describe block 'NEW FINDING: three-way same-family basket fusion is only PARTIALLY split by the deterministic coverage layer' and its cross-family sibling block immediately below it - both pass against current, unmodified production code, i.e. both directly document the ACTUAL (defective) behavior.
task2_newFindingDetail.whyThisWasNotCaughtByWorkstreamD: 06-claim-identity-v2.json's own 9-case adversarial matrix, and the prior BLOCKER-8 certification's own 8-case matrix, both exclusively construct 2-claim fusions (one conjunction, two sides). Neither matrix ever tests a 3+-claim, doubly-conjoined, un-enumerated sentence - a real (if less common than the 2-way case) drafting pattern in dense covenant prose (e.g. 'may incur Indebtedness under Facility A, or under Facility B, or under Facility C, in each case up to $X/$Y/$Z').
task2_newFindingDetail.isThisNewToWorkstreamD: NO - independently confirmed via the cross-family 3-way probe (task1 construction 'a-cross' above) that this single-split limitation already existed in findCoordinateClauseSplit's cross-family branch BEFORE Workstream D touched this file (that branch is documented as UNCHANGED by 06-claim-identity-v2.json's own semanticCoverageLayer.mechanism field: 'findCoordinateClauseSplit's existing cross-family trigger is UNCHANGED (regression-safe)'). Workstream D's new same-family branch inherits this pre-existing structural limitation rather than introducing a new one. This recertification is the first to construct and confirm an N=3 adversarial case against either branch.
task2_newFindingDetail.practicalImpactAssessment: Bounded, not catastrophic: (1) the discovery layer (Pass C/D) - which is the layer that actually feeds the compiler and, per 06-claim-identity-v2.json's own compatibility finding, the only layer with any live application wiring at all right now - does NOT share this limitation, since it operates per-Pass-B-item rather than by re-splitting fused prose; a well-behaved Pass B call that itself emits N separate WireRule items (as its own prompt instructs: 'List EVERY one you can find') produces N distinct discoveryIds regardless of N. (2) The semantic-coverage layer's own gap under-splits (produces fewer, coarser units) rather than over-splits or mis-attributes - the safe-failure verification gate (lib/contract-model/compiler/safe-failure/identity.ts) is documented as preferring semanticUnitId when available; a conflated 3-claim unit could under-credit (fail to separately verify) 2 of the 3 real claims, which is the SAME conservative-failure-direction (under-credit, never falsely over-credit) every other disclosed residual in this defect's history already carries - not a new failure DIRECTION, only a new failure TRIGGER shape (N=3 instead of N=2) not previously enumerated.
task2_newFindingDetail.recommendedScope: A future remediation should make findCoordinateClauseSplit (or its caller, hypothesizeUnitsForRegion) recurse into whichever side(s) it returns, re-applying the same split logic until no further qualifying split point exists - a bounded, deterministic loop (the same discipline this codebase already applies elsewhere, e.g. splitEnumeratedItems' own multi-item design), never attempted here per this phase's PRODUCTION-FROZEN mandate (Part B may not modify any production file).

task3_neverHashesRawAIParaphrase.purpose: Directly verify the code path where a distinguishing quote is accepted, with a concrete test proving a purely AI-PARAPHRASED (non-source-verbatim) distinguishing signal is REJECTED, not silently accepted.
task3_neverHashesRawAIParaphrase.codePathExamined: lib/contract-model/compiler/value-anchors.ts's verifyDistinguishingQuote, called from lib/contract-model/compiler/discovery/pass-c-neighborhood.ts line 176 (`verifyDistinguishingQuote(item.distinguishingQuote, anchorFullText)`) - the ONLY call site anywhere in the codebase where a distinguishing quote is accepted into identity (grep-confirmed: `grep -rn verifyDistinguishingQuote lib/` returns exactly this one production call site plus its own definition).
task3_neverHashesRawAIParaphrase.directUnitTest: verifyDistinguishingQuote('the short-term revolving credit line borrowings', sourceText) === null ; verifyDistinguishingQuote('the long-term amortizing term loan facility', sourceText) === null - both are semantically faithful PARAPHRASES of real source language ('Revolving Facility' / 'Term Facility') but neither is a verbatim substring, and both are correctly rejected.
task3_neverHashesRawAIParaphrase.endToEndTest: Two same-family/same-role/same-node candidates (Revolving Facility vs Term Facility Indebtedness prohibition, the EXACT non-numeric residual shape this whole workstream was built to address) whose ONLY attempted distinguishing signal is this pair of non-verbatim paraphrased distinguishingQuote values COLLIDE to a single discoveryId (verifiedQuoteFingerprint undefined on the resulting candidate) - proving the paraphrase was discarded, not hashed, and confirming the system fails CLOSED (falls back to the pre-existing V1 family-only behavior) rather than accepting a weak/unverified signal.
task3_neverHashesRawAIParaphrase.contrastTest: The IDENTICAL fused sentence, given a genuine VERBATIM quote for each side ('Indebtedness under the Revolving Facility' / 'Indebtedness under the Term Facility', both copied exactly from the source), correctly produces 2 distinct discoveryIds - proving the mechanism is fully functional when (and only when) the signal is real, source-grounded text, never mere wording similarity or paraphrase quality.
task3_neverHashesRawAIParaphrase.conclusion: CONFIRMED - the 'never hashes raw AI paraphrase' claim holds under direct adversarial attack. The single production call site enforces verbatim-substring verification before any quote can influence identity; a semantically-faithful but non-verbatim paraphrase is provably discarded rather than silently accepted.

task4_versionBumpCacheInvalidation.purpose: Verify DISCOVERY_PROMPT_VERSION and the semantic-coverage version constants actually invalidate any relevant cache/persisted-identity path, so stale pre-V2 identity results cannot silently persist forward.
task4_versionBumpCacheInvalidation.findingOnActualCacheArchitecture: This codebase has NO separate discovery-result or semantic-coverage-result cache keyed by these version strings as an independent invalidation lookup. Instead - and this is a STRONGER guarantee than a conventional cache-invalidation check - both version constants are DIRECT HASH INPUTS to the identity strings themselves (discoveryId and semanticUnitId), which are in turn the ONLY things ever persisted (as ClaimReviewItem.claimKey, via the `su:`/`cr:` prefixed forms in lib/contract-model/compiler/safe-failure/identity.ts). A version bump therefore does not need a separate cache-staleness check to take effect - it is structurally impossible for a pre-bump identity string to collide with a post-bump one, because the version string is baked directly into the hash.
evidenceChain: lib/contract-model/compiler/discovery/pass-c-neighborhood.ts line 232: discoveryId = computeStableKey('discovery-candidate', documentId, normalizedSourceRef, role, discoveryRunVersion, computeCandidateContentFingerprint(c)) - discoveryRunVersion is a direct positional hash input.

lib/contract-model/compiler/discovery/pipeline.ts: DISCOVERY_RUN_VERSION = `${DISCOVERY_PIPELINE_VERSION}+${DISCOVERY_PROMPT_VERSION}` = 'phase-2b-discovery-pipeline.v4+phase-2b-discovery.v3' (both bumped by Workstream D, confirmed by direct import in the new test file).

lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-coverage/identity.ts line 30: computeSemanticUnitId = hashParts([...sortedAnchorKeys, normalizeForIdentity(detectionSignature), SEMANTIC_COVERAGE_ALGORITHM_VERSION]) - the version constant is a direct positional hash input.

lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-coverage/types.ts: SEMANTIC_COVERAGE_ALGORITHM_VERSION = 'phase-3f1-semantic-coverage.v4' (bumped from v3 by Workstream D, confirmed by direct import in the new test file).

lib/contract-model/compiler/safe-failure/identity.ts: claimKeyFromSemanticUnit returns `su:${semanticUnitId}` and claimKeyFromCandidateRef returns `cr:${candidateRef}` verbatim, with only a namespace-prefix transformation - no independent re-keying formula exists that could itself drift out of sync with the underlying id's own versioning.
task4_versionBumpCacheInvalidation.directTest: runPassCNeighborhoodExpansion was called twice with byte-identical content but two different discoveryRunVersion strings (a synthetic pre-Workstream-D-shaped 'v3+v2' string vs the current real DISCOVERY_RUN_VERSION) - the resulting discoveryIds differ, proving the version string is a genuinely load-bearing hash input, not unused documentation.
task4_versionBumpCacheInvalidation.separateDiscoveryCacheCheck: computeDiscoveryInputHash (pipeline.ts) is DEFINED but has ZERO call sites anywhere in the codebase outside its own file (grep-confirmed) - there is no live discovery-level result cache to invalidate at all today; the orchestrator (lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts) calls runDiscoveryPipeline fresh on every run. This means the version-bump discipline's real, currently-load-bearing effect is entirely at the persisted-identity level (claimKey), not at any discovery-cache level - consistent with, and independently reconfirming, 06-claim-identity-v2.json's own freshVerification finding that zero ClaimReviewItem rows exist in this environment (there is, today, nothing FOR a stale cache to serve).
task4_versionBumpCacheInvalidation.semanticCompilerCacheNote: The one REAL, live in-memory cache in this subsystem (lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/cache.ts's InMemorySemanticCompilationCache) is keyed by computeCacheKey, which includes `candidateRef` (input.candidateRef) as a direct hash component - since candidateRef is derived from discoveryId for a Phase 2B candidate, a version-bumped discoveryId automatically produces a different candidateRef and therefore a different cache key, correctly invalidating any hypothetical stale entry without any additional wiring.
task4_versionBumpCacheInvalidation.conclusion: CONFIRMED, with a more precise mechanism than 'cache invalidation': there is no separate cache to invalidate for discovery/coverage identity; correctness instead rests on the version constants being genuine hash inputs to the persisted identity strings themselves, which this recertification directly proved (not merely inspected) by producing two different discoveryIds from two different version strings over identical content.

BLOCKER-8.rationale: The original BLOCKER-8 defect (two claims fused in one un-enumerated sentence colliding to one identity) remains CORRECTLY REMEDIATED for the 2-way case at both identity layers, independently reconfirmed by this recertification's own task6 regression check with zero reliance on the prior phase's own self-report. However, this recertification's own fresh adversarial construction (task1/task2) discovered a genuine, reproducible, currently-uncorrected defect within the SAME defect family at N=3: a sentence fusing THREE independently-operative, distinctly-numbered claims is only PARTIALLY separated by the deterministic semantic-coverage layer (2 units produced, not 3 - the 2nd and 3rd claims remain conflated into one semanticUnitId despite each carrying its own distinguishing, source-grounded number). This is a real instance of BLOCKER-8's own named defect class (two distinct claims sharing one identity despite being genuinely separable on their own numeric evidence), not covered by, and materially different from, the previously-disclosed AUDIT-F4-RESIDUAL-1 (which requires ZERO number on both sides). Per this phase's charter, BLOCKER-8 cannot be marked CERTIFIED_CLOSED while a genuine, freshly-confirmed instance of its own defect class remains open and undisclosed by the prior artifact.

AUDIT-F4.rationale: AUDIT-F4's required outcome is 'a generalized, source-grounded claim identity that does not conflate distinct propositions sharing family/role/node.' Task1/task2 above directly falsify the UNCONDITIONAL/GENERALIZED framing 06-claim-identity-v2.json applies to its own same-family fix ('an unconditional, always-active closure of the numeric-anchored same-family case') - the fix is conditional on there being exactly one fusion point in the sentence; a second fusion point (N=3 claims) is not closed, and this gap was neither tested for nor disclosed anywhere in that artifact's adversarialMatrix or disclosedResidual sections. Every OTHER claim independently re-tested by this recertification held under adversarial attack (task1 constructions b/c/d; task3's paraphrase-rejection proof; task4's version-bump proof; task5's residual-boundary reconfirmation) - so this disposition reflects one specific, narrow, precisely-bounded new finding (PART-B-BLOCKER8-FINDING-1), not a wholesale rejection of Workstream D's work. AUDIT-F4 cannot be marked CERTIFIED_CLOSED while this newly-confirmed, undisclosed gap remains unremediated and undisclosed in the artifact this recertification was asked to certify.

summaryForCaller: Recertification independently re-verified 7 of 8 attempted falsification vectors and found Workstream D's CLAIM IDENTITY V2 work holds up under fresh adversarial attack: genuinely-different value TYPES (dollar vs ratio) correctly split; dates are never mistaken for distinguishing anchors; hallucinated AI-authored numbers are genuinely rejected by extractGroundedValueAnchors, not trusted; a purely AI-paraphrased (non-verbatim) distinguishingQuote is directly proven to be rejected rather than silently hashed; version-bump correctness is confirmed via a direct, stronger-than-claimed mechanism (the version constants are hash inputs to the persisted identity itself, not a separate invalidatable cache); the disclosed AUDIT-F4-RESIDUAL-1 is reconfirmed exactly as narrow as claimed across 3 fresh sentences; and the ORIGINAL BLOCKER-8 certified collision case still correctly splits under the current V2 machinery with no regression. However, one genuine, previously-undisclosed, reproducible gap was found and is reported honestly rather than suppressed: findCoordinateClauseSplit performs at most one split per region, so a THREE-OR-MORE-way fused, un-enumerated, same-family-or-cross-family sentence (a real if less common drafting pattern) is only partially separated by the deterministic coverage layer, silently re-conflating the 2nd and later claims even when each carries its own distinguishing number. This directly falsifies the 'unconditional... always-active closure' framing applied to the same-family fix and is squarely inside AUDIT-F4's own frozen defect class. Both BLOCKER-8 and AUDIT-F4 are therefore dispositioned STILL_OPEN, not CERTIFIED_CLOSED, pending a future remediation that makes the coordinate-clause splitter recurse to a fixed point rather than stopping after one split - which this Part-B, production-frozen recertification is not permitted to implement itself.
